messages.content:
You write original English listening practice texts for Taiwanese students (high school or university). Each text is read aloud by text-to-speech, then the student types each sentence from dictation and repeats it aloud.
Write natural, spoken English with correct standard spelling. Give the text a short English title.
Return the text as lines: one sentence per line for a monologue; for a dialogue, one speaker's turn per line, alternating between two people, with no speaker names or labels.
Keep each sentence about 5 to 25 words. Write numbers, times, and amounts the way they are usually written (9:30, $15, 20%).
Do not write about real people, real brands, or real current events; invent names and details. Keep it appropriate for students.
Match the requested level, length (in words), and format. If a topic or keywords are given (in any language), build the text around them.
Also give titleZh, the title in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan usage), and subtitle, one Traditional Chinese sentence of at most 30 characters saying what the listener will hear.
In any Chinese text, write digits and Latin letters half-width (4號月台), never full-width.
{"topic":"","scenario":"a student describing a club fair on campus","level":"CEFR B1: everyday vocabulary, some longer sentences","words":150,"format":"monologue"}

message.content: {"title":"Campus Club Fair","titleZh":"校園社團展覽會","subtitle":"你會聽到學生描述社團展覽會的經過。","lines":["Last Saturday I spent the afternoon walking around the club fair on campus.","The weather was warm and there was a light breeze that made the tents feel comfortable.","Many student groups set up colorful booths along the main walkway near the library.","First I stopped at the photography club booth because I like taking pictures in my free time.","They showed some large prints and explained how they organize photo walks every weekend.","Next I visited the environmental club and signed up for a tree planting event next month.","A few music clubs played live songs, and small crowds gathered to listen and clap.","I chatted with members of the debate team who invited me to watch a practice session.","They also offered tips on public speaking and critical thinking for beginners.","Around mid-afternoon a food stall sold homemade cookies and lemonade for only $2 each.","I met some new friends from the art club and we swapped contact information.","Before leaving I picked up a flyer about volunteer tutoring for local children.","Everyone seemed friendly and excited to welcome new members to their activities.","The club fair was a great way to learn about campus life and meet people with similar interests.","I plan to attend two club meetings next week to see which one fits me best."]}
